definition_short: The side to move has no legal move and is NOT in check. The game is drawn immediately.
definition_long:
FIDE Art. 5.2.1: 'The game is drawn when the player to move has no legal move and his/her king is not in check. The game is said to end in stalemate. This immediately ends the game...'

The absence of check is what separates stalemate from checkmate, and it is a draw regardless of material. A player a queen ahead who stalemates has drawn. This makes stalemate a defensive RESOURCE, not merely an accident, and one of the main reasons endgame technique requires care rather than force.
epistemic_note: Official rule. Its status as a draw rather than a win is a rule choice, not a logical necessity — some historical and regional variants scored it differently.

origin.notes: The rule that stalemate is a draw was not universal historically; it has been scored as a win and as a loss in various times and places. Not yet researched for this record.

preconditions: The side to move has zero legal moves
That side's king is not in check

limitations: Being drawn regardless of material makes it a deliberate defensive device; an explanation should treat a stalemate trick as a resource, not a blunder by the winner.

explanation_templates.beginner: The player to move has no legal move at all, but is not in check. That is stalemate, and the game is a draw — no matter who was winning.
explanation_templates.intermediate: Stalemate: no legal move and no check, so the game is drawn. Watch for it whenever you are converting a large material advantage.
explanation_templates.advanced: Art. 5.2.1. A standing defensive resource in simplified endings.
